testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

unverified.claim: Both renamed tests still discriminate: removing the `-x` letter from CLAIM_WORKTREE reds the 'hand-made worktree' test, and removing it from CLAIM_BRANCH reds the 'two claims on one ticket' test. The whitespace-only mutation stays green. No gap found.
unverified.evidence: red: node --test --test-name-pattern=hand-made tests/stranded.test.mjs → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'a hand-made worktree `.worktrees/<N>-impl-<N>-<x>` is still a claim's worktree'; baseline: same cmd → exit 0, tests 1 pass 1 fail 0 cancelled 0. red: node --test --test-name-pattern=two.claims.on.one.ticket tests/stranded.test.mjs → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'a branch with no worktree is a claim too; two claims on one ticket are both listed, and its issue is read once'; baseline: same cmd → exit 0, tests 1 pass 1 fail 0 cancelled 0. The whitespace-only CLAIM_BRANCH mutation was added after the other two and I did not read its result; I did not use it in any claim.

unverified.claim: The stranded.mjs header (lines 37-42) still describes implementer claims as `.worktrees/<N>-impl-<N>[-x]`, `implementer/<N>-impl-<N>[-x]` and a `release-ticket.sh <N> impl-<N>[-x] implementer` dry run. The PR edits the comment at the CLAIM_WORKTREE constants in the same file to say no fleet path writes `-x`, so the two comments now disagree.
unverified.evidence: sed -n 34,44p plugin/scripts/stranded.mjs shows the `[-x]` forms at lines 37, 38 and 42. The diff's new comment at ~line 202 says '-x retry letter that no fleet path writes'.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reword the header to name the `-x` form as hand-made only, or drop `[-x]` from the header.

unverified.claim: Untouched evict.mjs still describes claim trees as `<N>-impl-<N>[-x]` on `implementer/<N>-impl-<N>[-x]` (lines 17 and 303, the latter in a user-facing kept-reason string) with no note that `-x` is never written. This conflicts with the new claim-ticket.sh and stranded.mjs comments and with CONTEXT.md's one-claim-per-ticket sentence. ADR 0036 line 19 has the same text.
unverified.evidence: grep -rn 'impl-<N>\[-x\]' on the snapshot: evict.mjs:17, evict.mjs:303, docs/adr/0036-an-idle-claim-tree-is-evicted-its-dependencies-go-the-claim-stays.md:19.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add the same 'a hand-made name only' qualifier at evict.mjs:17 or leave as an accepted regex-shape description. The code at 303 is user-visible text, so changing it is not a comment-only edit.
